title: Add interaction with JavaScript
learningObjectives: Complete add interaction with javascript using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: JavaScript should enhance meaningful HTML controls with clear event handling, state updates, validation, and feedback. Keep application logic separate from DOM rendering where practical and use textContent or safe DOM methods for dynamic text.
understand.whyItMatters: A useful interaction has a clear input, state transition, and result. Unstructured event handlers can create hidden dependencies and unsafe DOM updates.
understand.analogy: JavaScript is the control system that responds to user actions and updates the interface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The button event updates a status message using textContent. A production app should also persist completion through a trusted, appropriately designed data layer.

practise.guidedTask: Add one meaningful interaction to your page. Define its initial state, user action, result, validation, and accessible feedback.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
